claims.text: This trip is on-demand and its record carries no scheduled pickup time (trip_record.scheduled_at is null); the derived driver_deadline block states that the deadline cannot be fixed for that reason, and POL-NS-24's own note directs that where the record carries none POL-GEN-26 applies. POL-NS-24 measures the driver's lateness against the scheduled pickup time plus 5 minutes, so the driver's own timing obligation on this trip cannot be tested against the evidence at all: the booking was requested at 08:22:10 and arrival is recorded at 08:29:10, with no scheduled baseline to measure that gap against. That is a fact a rule of this version needs and the record cannot establish, so the case should be escalated and the 5.00 SGD held rather than collected.

The fee ultimately rests on the assertion that the rider was not at the pickup, and no artifact on this record establishes that assertion independently. The driver-device trace EV-GPS-05059 carries 25 fixes and not one for the rider - rider_track is empty and no rider_presence block is returned - so the record contains no rider-side location evidence either way. The platform's 'rider not on board' line and the RIDER_NO_SHOW reason code are entries in the same trip record the platform itself wrote, and the only human account on the file is the driver's own statement. Because the fact the no-show characterisation depends on cannot be established from independent evidence, POL-GEN-26 requires the open question to go to a human reviewer rather than being resolved by inference from the platform's own wait clock.

The driver's contact is carried by an artifact that is not clean, and the rider says so plainly: EV-CHAT-05059 is IMPAIRED, its issue code is UNREAD_MESSAGE, and its weight_multiplier is 0.85 - both messages were delivered but read_at is null on each, so the rider never opened them, and the rider's account that he 'did not even see his message' is corroborated by the record rather than contradicted by it. The rider accepts that the literal POL-NS-23 test is satisfied (a message sent at 08:29:30, a second at 08:32:45, and a call placed at 08:33:40 that rang 25 s unanswered, all before the 08:35:30 cancellation), and that the free-wait clock was served on the platform's own numbers (arrival 08:29:10, expiry 08:34:10, cancellation 08:35:30), so the rider's objection is to the contact itself, not to the length of the wait. But the deciding fact on that contact sits on an artifact below 1.0, and under POL-GEN-02(2) the confidence on the contact point cannot exceed 0.85.

The rider's suggestion that he was 'charged $5 again' is not supported by the record and the rider does not press it: EV-FARE-05059 is COMPLETE at weight 1.0, it carries exactly one cancellation-fee line of 5.00 SGD charged at 08:35:34 with refund_issued_sgd 0.00, and its lines reconcile to total_charged 5.00. The dispute turns on whether that single fee should stand, not on any duplicate charge.

On POL-GEN-03's vocabulary, ESCALATE is the only ruling available here that leaves the rider not carrying the disputed charge: the 5.00 SGD is presently CHARGED with no refund issued, escalation holds that amount while a human reviewer takes the file, whereas NO_ACTION would leave the charge standing and collected (and DRIVER_COMPENSATION would confirm the transfer to the driver). POL-NS-26 makes the AI's no-show ruling final but expressly subjects it to POL-GEN-26, so escalation remains open in this category, and it is the outcome the gaps in this record require.

claims.text: The driver's free wait is satisfied on the face of the record: POL-NS-21 runs the clock from the driver's arrival at the pickup, the auto-arrival event is recorded at 2026-08-27T08:29:10+08:00, and the driver cancelled at 08:35:30 — 380 seconds after arrival against the 300-second free wait the clause fixes, some 80 seconds past expiry. The cancellation was therefore a permissible rider no-show.

The arrival that starts the free-wait clock is itself corroborated under the policy's arrival test: the driver-device trace carries 25 fixes across the whole 08:23:05–08:35:05 window at 100% coverage with no gap longer than 30 s, its nearest fix to the pickup is 6.55 m away at 08:30:05, well inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, and from 08:29:05 onward every fix at that spot reports speed 0 kph — so the driver was physically at the pickup for the entire waiting period, not merely flagged as arrived.

The driver's contact obligation under POL-NS-23 is met. Two in-app messages were sent to the rider at 08:29:30 and 08:32:45, and an in-app call was placed at 08:33:40 that rang unanswered for 25 seconds — both a message and a call before the 08:35:30 cancellation. I disclose that the chat log EV-CHAT-05059 is IMPAIRED at weight 0.85 with issue code UNREAD_MESSAGE; that impairment concerns whether the rider opened the messages (read_at is null), not whether the driver sent them (delivery is recorded at 08:29:31 and 08:32:47), and the trip record independently carries chat_message_count 2 and the in_app_calls entry.

The rider's complaint that she 'did not even see his message' raises no defence under POL-NS-23. The clause requires the driver to have sent at least one in-app chat message and placed at least one in-app call before cancelling; it imposes no obligation on the rider to read or answer either, and both acts are on the record before trip_record.cancelled_at.

The rider's assertion that the driver 'cancelled too fast' is contradicted by the trace: the driver's fixes sit stationary at the pickup point from 08:29:05 through 08:35:05, a dwell of roughly six minutes, and the cancellation came after the 300-second free wait had run out. On this record the driver waited longer than POL-NS-21 requires, not less.

The fee charged is exactly the fee the policy fixes: 5.00 SGD, equal to policy_fee_sgd of 5.00, with payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00. POL-NS-22 provides that a fee charged after a compliant free wait is transferred to the driver as compensation for time and fuel, so the ruling should be DRIVER_COMPENSATION with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both 5.00 — the money the ruling moves to the driver under POL-GEN-03's definition of that outcome.

The rider cannot make out POL-NS-24. Its only charge-triggering condition is a driver who fails to arrive by the scheduled pickup time plus 5 minutes, and this trip is on-demand with no scheduled time: the record's driver_deadline block returns deadline null with the reason 'on-demand trip: no scheduled time'. The deadline the clause needs cannot be fixed against this driver, and what the record does show is arrival 6 minutes 35 seconds after assignment and a wait past the free wait — no late-arrival breach on which the clause could operate.

POL-GEN-26 does not escalate this case. Every fact the no-show rules need — when the driver arrived, whether he messaged and called before cancelling, and whether the free wait ran — is carried by artifacts that are COMPLETE at weight 1.0, and the only absent artifact, the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-05059-01, is MISSING at weight 0.0 and under POL-GEN-02(3) carries no fact at all. No rule bearing on these facts requires a traffic advisory, so there is no open question for a human reviewer to resolve.

rider_profile.no_show_cancellations_30d stands at 3, and counting this trip if its fee stands takes it to 4, so POL-NS-25's threshold of 3 is reached and the rider's account should be referred for review under that clause (mandatory upfront payment, temporary suspension pending Trust & Safety review). This is a referral that sits alongside the money; it never changes the ruling on this trip.

This is an AI-final case. The contested amount is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD threshold, and neither profile carries a fraud flag (both fraud_flags are 0), so no 0.95 confidence bar is raised and no escalation arises; POL-NS-26's finality for a no-show at this value applies, subject only to safety and to POL-GEN-26, neither of which is engaged.

Both profiles carry history that could be waved at in argument — the driver's prior_no_show_flags and no_show_terminations_30d, the rider's no_show_disputes_30d and cancellation_rate — but under POL-GEN-01 every profile field other than the two fraud_flags fields and rider_profile.no_show_cancellations_30d is context only and may never ground a finding. The outcome must be read off this trip's own timestamps, trace and ledger, which is where the driver's case rests.

ruling.explanation: To the rider: your claim is not supported on this record. The driver's arrival at the pickup is recorded at 08:29:10 (EV-TRIP-05059) and is corroborated by his own device trace (EV-GPS-05059), which sits stationary on the pickup point from 08:29:05 through 08:35:05. POL-NS-21 gives the driver a free wait of 300 seconds from arrival, so the wait expired at 08:34:10; the driver cancelled at 08:35:30, 380 seconds after arrival, some 80 seconds past expiry. Before cancelling he sent two in-app messages (08:29:30 and 08:32:45) and placed an in-app call (08:33:40, unanswered, ringing 25 s), all before the cancellation, so POL-NS-23's contact obligation — at least one message and at least one call before cancelling — is met and the fee is not voided. The only charge on the ledger (EV-FARE-05059) is a single cancellation fee of 5.00 SGD, equal to the policy fee of 5.00, with no refund issued and no second charge, so there is no duplicate to return. You are right that the chat log (EV-CHAT-05059) is impaired — weight 0.85, issue UNREAD_MESSAGE, the messages were delivered but never opened — and I have taken that into account: it is the fact the contact limb reads that caps my confidence, and my confidence does not exceed 0.85. Your escalation argument is rejected. POL-NS-24 measures a driver's lateness against a scheduled pickup time plus five minutes; this was an on-demand booking with no scheduled time, so that clause has no trigger at all and no fact the deciding rules need is missing — when the driver arrived, whether he messaged and called before cancelling, and whether the free wait ran are all carried by evidence at weight 1.0 (EV-TRIP-05059 and EV-GPS-05059). No rule requires rider-side location evidence: the no-show limbs test the driver's wait and his contact attempts, not proof that you were absent, and nothing in your account (that you did not see the message) denies that the driver waited and tried. The missing traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-05059-01) has weight 0.0 and carries no fact, and no no-show rule needs one. ESCALATE is not available here: POL-GEN-26 is not engaged and POL-NS-26 makes the AI ruling on a 5.00 SGD no-show final. To the driver: the fee stands. Under POL-NS-22 a no-show fee charged after a compliant free wait is transferred to you as compensation for time and fuel, so the ruling is DRIVER_COMPENSATION and both amount fields carry the 5.00 SGD the ruling moves (fee_charged_sgd 5.00 = policy_fee_sgd 5.00, EV-FARE-05059). The fee charged is exactly 5.00 SGD, so POL-NS-22's fee-amount referral does not fire. Your own history, and the rider's, is context only under POL-GEN-01 and has played no part in this outcome, which is read off this trip's own timestamps, trace and ledger. One referral applies: the rider's no-show count reaches POL-NS-25's threshold of 3 with this trip counted, so the account is flagged for review.

ruling.explanation: To the rider: your SGD 5.00 no-show charge for trip TRP-05059 is not refunded today, and it is not upheld today either — the case goes to a human reviewer and the SGD 5.00 stays held rather than collected or refunded. Two of your points are settled against you on the record. On 'cancelled too fast': the driver arrived at Block 401, Ang Mo Kio Avenue 10 at 08:29:10, and the driver-device trace (EV-GPS-05059, COMPLETE) corroborates that arrival — its nearest fix is 6.5 m from the pickup, inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, and the trace is stationary there from 08:29 — so POL-NS-21's free wait of 300 s ran out at 08:34:10 and cancellation came at 08:35:30, 380 s after arrival, some 80 s past expiry. On 'did not even see his message': POL-NS-23 requires the driver to send at least one in-app message and place at least one in-app call before cancelling; it does not require you to read or answer. Two messages (08:29:30 and 08:32:45) and one call (08:33:40, ringing 25 s unanswered) are on the record before the 08:35:30 cancellation. The fare ledger (EV-FARE-05059, COMPLETE) carries one cancellation-fee line of SGD 5.00 charged at 08:35:34 with refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so there was no second charge. To the driver: POL-NS-21 and POL-NS-23 are met and the SGD 5.00 is exactly the fee POL-NS-22 fixes, but the fee cannot be confirmed on this record. POL-NS-24 refunds the fee where the driver failed to arrive by the scheduled pickup time plus 5 minutes, and its own note says that where an on-demand trip's record carries no scheduled time and the deadline cannot be fixed, POL-GEN-26 applies. This trip is on-demand: scheduled_at is null and the record's driver-deadline block returns deadline null for the reason 'on-demand trip: no scheduled time'. The late-arrival question POL-NS-24 raises therefore cannot be answered from this record, and POL-GEN-26 requires the case to go to a human reviewer with that open question stated, rather than an outcome being inferred from the gap; your own claim that the deadline 'cannot be fixed' concedes the fact that puts the case there. On the claims: the fee-stands claims (free wait served on the 380 s dwell, arrival corroborated by the trace, contact made, SGD 5.00 equal to policy_fee_sgd, and the AI-finality argument under POL-GEN-22/POL-NS-26) are accepted on the merits, but none of them resolves POL-NS-24, and POL-NS-26 itself makes no-show finality subject to POL-GEN-26, so they do not carry a DRIVER_COMPENSATION ruling today. The rider's claim that the empty rider side of the trace (rider_track empty) leaves the no-show unproven is rejected: no clause of this version requires rider-side location evidence — the no-show test is the driver's wait under POL-NS-21, read off the trip record and the trace — and the escalation here rests on POL-NS-24/POL-GEN-26, not on that. The rider's point that the contact facts sit on the impaired chat log EV-CHAT-05059 (weight 0.85, issue UNREAD_MESSAGE) is accepted, and is why the confidence stated here is 0.85. The rider's suggestion that escalation is simply the outcome that spares the rider is not itself a ground — escalation follows only from POL-GEN-26, which is what produces it here. Both parties' profile history was correctly kept out of the outcome under POL-GEN-01, except rider_profile.no_show_cancellations_30d, which POL-NS-25 names for the referral above. The SGD 5.00 remains held pending review.

This referral never changes the ruling on the trip.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider: your dispute is not supported, so the 5.00 SGD no-show fee stands and the driver keeps it. To the driver: the fee is upheld and the 5.00 SGD is confirmed as your compensation under POL-NS-22. Here is how I read the record.

Wait (POL-NS-21). The free-wait clock runs from the driver's arrival at the pickup. The trip record EV-TRIP-05059 (weight 1.0, COMPLETE) puts the auto-arrival at 08:29:10, so the 300-second free wait expired at 08:34:10. The driver cancelled at 08:35:30 — 380 seconds after arrival, 80 seconds past expiry. The arrival is independently corroborated by the driver-device trace EV-GPS-05059 (weight 1.0, COMPLETE): 25 fixes over 08:23:05–08:35:05, nearest fix 6.55 m from the pickup (inside the 50 m STANDARD radius), and every fix from 08:29:05 onward stationary at 0 kph. So the driver was physically at the pickup and waited the full free period; your account that he "cancelled too fast" is contradicted by the trace.

Contact (POL-NS-23). The driver must have sent at least one in-app message and placed at least one in-app call before cancelling. The chat log EV-CHAT-05059 records messages at 08:29:30 and 08:32:45, and the trip record's in_app_calls records a call at 08:33:40 that rang 25 seconds unanswered — all before the 08:35:30 cancellation. I name the chat log's impairment: EV-CHAT-05059 is IMPAIRED, weight 0.85, issue code UNREAD_MESSAGE (both messages delivered, neither opened). Your point that you never saw the messages is consistent with that record, but it is not a defence: POL-NS-23 obliges the driver to send and call, not the rider to read or answer.

Fee (POL-NS-22 and POL-GEN-03). EV-FARE-05059 (weight 1.0, COMPLETE) shows exactly one cancellation-fee line of 5.00 SGD charged at 08:35:34, refund_issued_sgd 0.00, reconciling to total_charged 5.00 — equal to the policy fee of 5.00. Your suggestion of being "charged $5 again" is not supported: there is no duplicate charge. Because the fee stands on a compliant no-show, POL-NS-22 fixes the outcome as DRIVER_COMPENSATION, with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both 5.00 — the money the ruling moves to the driver.

POL-NS-24 (driver no-show) does not apply, so no refund arises under it and no 5.00 goodwill credit: its trigger is a driver arriving later than the scheduled pickup time plus 5 minutes, this was an on-demand trip with no scheduled time at all, and in any event the driver did not arrive late — the full free wait was served and he did attempt contact.

Escalation (POL-GEN-26) is refused. Every fact the no-show rules need is carried by COMPLETE artifacts at weight 1.0: when the driver arrived and how long he waited (trip record and GPS trace), and whether he messaged and called before cancelling (trip record and chat log). The scheduled pickup time is not a fact these rules need, because POL-NS-24 is not engaged. The only absent artifact, the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-05059-01, is MISSING at weight 0.0 and carries no fact; no rule here requires one. Your further point that no rider-side location evidence exists does not create an open question: the no-show is established by the full free wait elapsing without the rider boarding, on the platform's own clock plus the driver's account.

Party history is context only (POL-GEN-01): the profiles' ratings, cancellation rates and prior flags decide nothing here. The outcome is read from this trip's own timestamps, trace and ledger.

Confidence. Value 5.00 SGD is below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, no fraud flag is present, and POL-NS-26 makes the no-show ruling final — so no escalation bar arises. My confidence is 0.85, capped by POL-GEN-02(2): the message half of the POL-NS-23 contact fact rests on the impaired chat log EV-CHAT-05059 at 0.85, and its restatement in the trip record is not an independent carrier.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver: the 5.00 SGD no-show fee stands and is confirmed to the driver as compensation, so the rider's request for a refund is not granted.

THE WAIT. POL-NS-21 (the v2.1 free wait) runs its 5-minute clock from the driver's arrival at the pickup. EV-TRIP-05059 (weight 1.0) records the auto-arrival at 08:29:10 and the cancellation at 08:35:30 — 380 seconds against the 300-second free wait, 80 seconds past it. EV-GPS-05059 (weight 1.0) corroborates that arrival under the policy's arrival test: the nearest fix is 6.55 m from the pickup, inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, at a reported accuracy of 3 m, and the driver's fixes sit stationary at that point from 08:29:05 through 08:35:05. The rider's 'cancelled too fast' is not made out; the driver waited longer than the policy requires.

THE CONTACT. POL-NS-23 (v2.1 2.3) requires a message and a call before cancelling. EV-TRIP-05059 records two messages (08:29:30 and 08:32:45) and a call placed at 08:33:40 that rang 25 s unanswered — all before the 08:35:30 cancellation — so that obligation is met. We accept the rider's point that the chat log EV-CHAT-05059 is impaired, at weight 0.85 with issue code UNREAD_MESSAGE: both messages were delivered but never opened. That impairment goes only to whether the rider read them, not to whether the driver sent them, so it does not void the fee; it does cap our confidence at 0.85 under POL-GEN-02(2), and POL-GEN-02(3) requires us to name it.

THE FEE. EV-FARE-05059 (weight 1.0) carries a single cancellation-fee line of 5.00 SGD, matching the policy fee of 5.00, charged with no refund issued; the suggestion of a second charge is not supported by the record. Because the fee stands, POL-NS-22 fixes the outcome as DRIVER_COMPENSATION, with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both 5.00 — the one figure the ruling moves, not a second payment.

THE RIDER'S ESCALATION ARGUMENTS. (a) POL-NS-24 cannot be made out on an on-demand trip: the record carries no scheduled pickup time (driver_deadline.deadline is null, reason 'on-demand trip: no scheduled time'), so the lateness test that clause states cannot run. We have considered its note pointing to POL-GEN-26, but POL-GEN-26 escalates only where a fact a rule needs cannot be established because the evidence that would carry it is missing or impaired. The trip record and the GPS trace are both COMPLETE at 1.0 and carry every fact the no-show rules need — when the driver arrived, whether he messaged and called before cancelling, and that the free wait ran. No outcome has been inferred from the absence of a scheduled time, and POL-NS-26 leaves the no-show ruling to the AI here. (b) The absence of rider-side location evidence raises no open question either: POL-NS-21 conditions the driver's right to cancel on the free wait, and the platform's own records — the wait_timer_expired event at 08:34:15 and the RIDER_NO_SHOW reason code — carry that the wait ran out with the rider not on board; no clause requires independent rider-presence evidence. (c) ESCALATE would hold the fee, but no clause on this record produces it.

PROFILES. We have used neither party's history to decide this trip. Under POL-GEN-01 only the two fraud_flags fields and rider_profile.no_show_cancellations_30d may be cited, and only for the rules that name them; every other profile field is context only.

REFERRAL. POL-NS-25: the rider's profile carries no_show_cancellations_30d of 3, and counting this trip, whose fee stands, the count is 3 or more, so the rider's account is referred for review — mandatory upfront payment and temporary suspension pending Trust & Safety review. This referral does not change the money outcome on this trip.

CONFIDENCE. 0.85, capped by the impaired chat log EV-CHAT-05059 (weight 0.85, UNREAD_MESSAGE). The contested amount of 5.00 SGD is below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band and neither profile carries a fraud flag, so no higher bar applies and the case is AI-final.
